articles.title: Astro Definitions for April Fools Day
articles.summary: This article combines current astronomical news and humorous redefinitions of celestial terms under the "April Fools Day" theme, discussing topics like supernovae rates, Martian auroras, water geysers on Enceladus, and the Deep Impact mission. It also includes a serious call for amateur astronomers to volunteer for Project ASTRO, an educational outreach program aimed at teaching fundamental astronomy concepts in classrooms.

articles.title: The Shallow Sky
articles.summary: Jupiter's Oval BA, a previously white spot, has recently grown and turned a faint reddish color, earning it informal names like "Red Jr." from astronomers. While the exact cause of the red color in Jovian storms remains a mystery, possibly linked to photochemical smog, observers are encouraged to watch Jupiter as it is now easily visible. The article also briefly mentions observing opportunities for Saturn, Mars, and the Moon.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association
articles.summary: This document provides a financial overview of the San Jose Astronomical Association for 2005, detailing income, expenses, and year-end account balances. Additionally, it offers an astronomical observing guide for April 2006, highlighting celestial objects visible in the morning sky like Venus, Mercury, and Comet Pojmanski, and announces a May 13 member meeting for eclipse presentations.

articles.title: Auction XXVI
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting its annual astronomical auction and swap meet at Houge Park in San Jose on Sunday, April 9, 2006. This event provides an opportunity for beginners to acquire their first telescope and for experienced observers to find specific equipment, with detailed rules provided for item registration, bidding, commission, and a subsequent swap meet. Attendees are encouraged to preregister items for free advertising and help promote the event to new astronomy enthusiasts.

articles.title: SJAA Yosemite Public Star Party 2006
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting its annual Yosemite Public Star Party on July 21 and 22 at Glacier Point. Participants receive free admission and camping in exchange for hosting two public observing events, with priority given to SJAA members. The event is scheduled around the new moon for optimal viewing conditions.

articles.title: Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture Series: Ron Marzke Talk
articles.summary: This document announces the Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture Series event on April 26, 2006, featuring Dr. Ron Marzke of San Francisco State University. Dr. Marzke will deliver a non-technical, illustrated talk titled "News from the Distant Past: How Galaxies Tell Their Stories," focusing on galaxy formation and evolution, including recent discoveries of massive galaxies in the early universe. Additionally, the document provides comprehensive Solar System statistics for April 2006, detailing Right Ascension, Declination, Distance, Magnitude, and Size for planets and the Sun.

articles.title: SJAA loaner scope status
articles.summary: This article details the status of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) loaner telescope program, listing a wide variety of telescopes and other observing equipment available to members. It provides contact information for Mike Koop to arrange immediate loans, outlines scopes currently on loan, and notes those with extended loan periods. Members are encouraged to inquire about the many available scopes.
